[[File:Chi bounded.svg|thumb|upright=0.8|A graph <math>G</math> that can be 4-colored, whose largest [[clique (graph theory)|clique]] is size 4.
<br /><br />
Families this graph belongs to include the [[perfect graph]]s, graphs of [[boxicity]] two, the [[circle graph|circle]] and [[polygon-circle graph]]s, and the [[even-hole-free graph]]s (specifically the '''even-cycle-free graphs''').]]

In [[graph theory]], a '''<math>\chi</math>-bounded''' (using the Greek letter [[chi (letter)|chi]]) family <math>\mathcal{F}</math> of graphs is one for which there is some function <math>f</math> such that, for every integer <math>t</math> the graphs in <math>\mathcal{F}</math> with <math>t=\omega(G)</math> ([[clique number]]) can be [[graph coloring|colored]] with at most <math>f(t)</math> colors. The function <math>f(t)</math> is called a '''<math>\chi</math>-binding function''' for <math>\mathcal{F}</math>. These concepts and their notations were formulated by [[András Gyárfás]].{{r|g87}} The use of the Greek letter [[Chi (letter)|chi]] in the term <math>\chi</math>-bounded is based on the fact that the [[chromatic number]] of a graph <math>G</math> is commonly denoted <math>\chi(G)</math>. An overview of the area can be found in a survey of Alex Scott and [[Paul Seymour (mathematician)|Paul Seymour]].{{r|survey}}

==Nontriviality==
It is not true that the family of all graphs is <math>\chi</math>-bounded.
As {{harvtxt|Descartes|1947}}, {{harvtxt|Zykov|1949}} and {{harvtxt|Mycielski|1955}} showed, there exist [[triangle-free graph]]s of arbitrarily large chromatic number,{{r|descartes|z|m}} so for these graphs it is not possible to define a finite value of <math>f(2)</math>.
Thus, <math>\chi</math>-boundedness is a nontrivial concept, true for some graph families and false for others.{{r|pkk}}

==Specific classes==
Every class of graphs of bounded [[chromatic number]] is (trivially) <math>\chi</math>-bounded, with <math>f(t)</math> equal to the bound on the chromatic number. This includes, for instance, the [[planar graph]]s, the [[bipartite graph]]s, and the graphs of bounded [[degeneracy (graph theory)|degeneracy]]. Complementarily, the graphs in which the [[independence number]] is bounded are also <math>\chi</math>-bounded, as [[Ramsey's theorem]] implies that they have large cliques.

[[Vizing's theorem]] can be interpreted as stating that the [[line graph]]s are <math>\chi</math>-bounded, with <math>f(t)=t+1</math>.{{r|cs|km}} The [[claw-free graph]]s more generally are also <math>\chi</math>-bounded with <math>f(t)\le t^2</math>. This can be seen by using Ramsey's theorem to show that, in these graphs, a vertex with many neighbors must be part of a large clique.
This bound is nearly tight in the worst case, but connected claw-free graphs that include three mutually-nonadjacent vertices have even smaller chromatic number, <math>f(t)=2t</math>.{{r|cs}}

Other <math>\chi</math>-bounded graph families include:
*The [[perfect graph]]s, with <math>f(t)=t</math>
*The graphs of [[boxicity]] two{{r|ag60}}, which is the [[intersection graph]]s of axis-parallel rectangles, with <math>f(t)\in O(t\log(t))</math>([[big O notation]]){{r|max}}
*The graphs of bounded [[clique-width]]{{r|dk12}}
*The [[intersection graph]]s of scaled and translated copies of any compact convex shape in the plane{{r|kkn04}}
*The [[polygon-circle graph]]s, with <math>f(t)=2^t</math>
*The [[circle graph]]s, with <math>f(t)=2t\log_2t+2\log_2\log_2t+10t</math>{{r|circ}} and (generalizing circle graphs) the "outerstring graphs", intersection graphs of bounded curves in the plane that all touch the unbounded face of the [[arrangement of lines|arrangement]] of the curves{{r|rw14}}
*The [[outerstring graph]] is an intersection graph of curves that lie in a common half-plane and have one endpoint on the boundary of that half-plane{{r|outer}}
*The [[intersection graph]]s of curves that cross a fixed curve between 1 and <math>n \in \N</math> times{{r|curv}}
*The [[even-hole-free graph]]s (or more precisely, the '''even-cycle-free graphs''', which is free of holes of length 4), with <math>f(t)=2t</math>, as every such graph has a [[bisimplicial vertex]], a vertex whose neighborhood is the union of two cliques{{r|evenhole}}

However, although intersection graphs of convex shapes, circle graphs, and outerstring graphs are all special cases of [[string graph]]s, the string graphs themselves are not <math>\chi</math>-bounded.
They include as a special case the intersection graphs of [[line segment]]s, which are also not <math>\chi</math>-bounded.{{r|pkk}}

==Unsolved problems==
{{unsolved|mathematics|Are all tree-free graph classes <math>\chi</math>-bounded?}}
According to the [[Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture]], for every [[Tree (graph theory)|tree]] <math>T</math>, the graphs that do not contain <math>T</math> as an [[induced subgraph]] are <math>\chi</math>-bounded. 
For instance, this would include the case of claw-free graphs, as a claw is a special kind of tree.
However, the conjecture is known to be true only for certain special trees, including [[Path graph|paths]]{{r|g87}} and radius-two trees.{{r|kp94}}

A <math>\chi</math>-bounded class of graphs is '''polynomially <math>\chi</math>-bounded''' if it has a <math>\chi</math>-binding function <math>f(t)</math> that grows at most polynomially as a function of <math>t</math>. As every <math>n</math>-vertex graph <math>G</math> contains an [[independent set (graph theory)|independent set]] with cardinality at least <math>n/\chi(G)</math>, all polynomially <math>\chi</math>-bounded classes have the [[Erdős–Hajnal conjecture|Erdős–Hajnal property]].
Another problem on <math>\chi</math>-boundedness was posed by Louis Esperet, who asked whether every hereditary class of graphs that is <math>\chi</math>-bounded is also polynomially <math>\chi</math>-bounded.{{r|km}} A strong counterexample to Esperet's conjecture was announced in 2022 by Briański, Davies, and Walczak, who proved that there exist <math>\chi</math>-bounded hereditary classes whose function <math>f(t)</math> can be chosen arbitrarily as long as it grows more quickly than a certain cubic polynomial.{{r|bdw}}
